name: Anti-racism
summary: Anti-racism is a set of ideas and actions aimed at countering racial prejudice, systemic racism and the oppression of racial groups, and at securing equal treatment and opportunity. It rejects doctrines of racial superiority as false, supports anti-discrimination law and time-limited special measures, and in its structural form judges policies by whether they reduce racial inequity. It has no economic or constitutional programme of its own, so most of its positions on other issues are inferred.
scope: Mainstream contemporary anti-racism as codified in the UN International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (1965), the nonviolent civil-rights tradition of Martin Luther King Jr., and the structural/institutional analysis of Carmichael and Hamilton and of Ibram X. Kendi. It excludes ethnic-nationalist movements such as Afrocentrism, and the radical anti-capitalist strand is noted but not taken as the core. Most statements outside race, discrimination and colonialism are inferred and marked low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Stokely Carmichael

universal-healthcare.rationale: Health care is one domain where institutional racism is documented, so adherents tend to favour guaranteed access; inferred, not a stated anti-racist demand.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The anti-capitalist strand ties racial inequality to economic inequality, so higher pay floors are usually welcomed; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Anti-racism has no settled view on markets as such; the socialist strand distrusts them while liberal strands do not.

public-ownership.rationale: Only the socialist strand takes a view on ownership; mainstream anti-racism is indifferent.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Kendi and socialist strands link racism to capitalism and wealth gaps, so progressive taxation is a natural inference.

unions-good.rationale: Anti-racist movements have often allied with labour; inferred from the economic-inequality strand rather than stated.

property-fundamental.rationale: ICERD lists the right to own property among rights to be enjoyed without racial distinction, but anti-racism does not rank it above redress.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Kendi links racism with capitalism, so tighter regulation of firms is a likely preference; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare cuts are usually seen as worsening racial disparities, so adherents mostly reject them; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only socialist-leaning anti-racists would endorse this; the ideology itself is silent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Concern about discriminatory policing makes adherents wary of expanded surveillance; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Racial disparities in drug enforcement are a standard criminal-justice complaint, so legalisation is commonly favoured; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: ICERD Article 4 requires states to make dissemination of racial-superiority ideas and incitement punishable, though some adherents, especially in the US, favour counter-speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Anti-racism relies on rule-of-law guarantees of equal treatment, which sit uneasily with leaders bypassing institutions; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Anti-racism looks to the state to prohibit and remedy discrimination (ICERD Art. 2), so calling it unnecessary and harmful contradicts its programme.

limit-guns.rationale: Anti-racism has no stated gun policy and adherents are divided between gun control and armed self-defence traditions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Policing is a main site of alleged institutional racism, so adherents resist giving it more power; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by anti-racism; adherents differ.

decide-locally.rationale: King's letter targets segregation maintained by local and state law, so adherents distrust purely local control; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Criminal-justice reform is part of modern anti-racism, and rehabilitation is the usual alternative to punitive sentencing; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anti-racism is usually part of a broader equal-rights outlook, but this is an inference, not a core claim.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a racial-equality question as such; inferred from the generally progressive alignment of adherents.

more-religion-public.rationale: King's movement was church-based while other anti-racists are secular, so adherents are split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: ICERD allows and calls for special measures to secure equal enjoyment of rights, and Kendi treats remedying past discrimination as the antiracist test.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Race is treated as socially constructed, and Kendi links racism to patriarchy; the gender claim is inferred by analogy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Anti-racism challenges claims that a dominant national culture deserves protection, though it values cultural recognition for minorities.

gradual-change.rationale: King's letter attacks the call to wait for a convenient season and the myth that time alone heals injustice, and Kendi demands immediate policy change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anti-racists generally see restriction as racially skewed, though ICERD itself leaves citizenship rules to states; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: ICERD is a UN treaty with a monitoring committee, so adherents tend to welcome international oversight; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between pro-trade and anti-capitalist views.

nation-first.rationale: ICERD frames racial discrimination as a matter of international concern, which fits poorly with putting national interest first; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents split between support for protecting victims and anti-colonial distrust of intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Many adherents criticise racialised border control, but ICERD leaves citizenship to states and open borders is not a core claim.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental racism is a common theme, so adherents tend to support strong action; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated position; concern about algorithmic bias is balanced by general indifference.

revolution-justified.rationale: King and ICERD favour nonviolent and legal change, while anti-colonial and Black Power strands accept revolution; adherents split.

experts-over-public.rationale: No stated position; adherents trust social-science findings on race but not technocracy as such.

central-planning.rationale: Only the socialist strand has a view; anti-racism as such is neutral.

socialized-markets.rationale: Only the socialist strand has a view; anti-racism as such is neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inherited wealth is a mechanism of the racial wealth gap, so adherents lean toward taxing it; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Seen as a way to narrow racial economic gaps and supported by many adherents; inferred rather than stated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed beyond targeted-investment arguments for disadvantaged communities.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only a small socialist wing would endorse this; mainstream anti-racism works within existing economies.

one-party-rule.rationale: ICERD guarantees equal political participation, which is incompatible with single-party leadership; inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rank conflicts with equal standing before the law; inferred, not a prominent anti-racist theme.

democracy-best.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(c) guarantees universal and equal suffrage, and the civil-rights tradition fought for the vote, though anti-racists stress that majorities can be unjust.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums can let majorities override minority rights, a worry in the civil-rights tradition; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Only the socialist strand has a view.

natural-rulers.rationale: ICERD calls doctrines of superiority based on racial differentiation false and condemnable, and the same logic rejects innate ruling classes.

political-violence-never.rationale: King's nonviolence contrasts with Black Power and anti-colonial strands, so adherents are split.

war-builds-character.rationale: ICERD links racial discrimination to threats to peace, and adherents rarely valorise war; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents include religious civil-rights traditions and secular ones; no stated position.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Equal treatment under secular law is the anti-racist standard, though no source addresses scripture directly; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(a) guarantees equal treatment before tribunals as a state duty; privatising justice is inferred to be opposed.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-colonial strands distrust great-power dominance; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: ICERD calls for integrationist multiracial movements and condemns policies built on ethnic superiority, which conflicts with ethnically defined nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Only the socialist strand holds this; the wider ideology does not.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Kendi defines racist policy by inequitable outcomes, and the structural view treats formal equal opportunity as insufficient.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Dispossession of Indigenous peoples is cited as institutional racism, so authority over traditional lands is a plausible remedy; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The article links reparations for colonisation to anti-racist and anti-colonial demands, though it presents this as one strand, not universal.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Anti-racism rests on equal moral worth and duty toward others; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The tradition is framed through individual and group rights against discrimination, so subordinating rights to duties is opposed; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Population control has historically been aimed at racial minorities, so adherents are wary; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No stated anti-racist position on the pace of technological change; adherents split between enthusiasm and bias concerns.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Concern that automated systems reproduce structural bias makes adherents sceptical; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: King criticises those who prefer order to justice, and the past order was one of segregation and hierarchy; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kendi judges policies by racial outcomes, but anti-racism is not pragmatic in general.

direct-action.rationale: King defends nonviolent direct action as necessary, though he used it alongside legal and electoral means rather than instead of them.

means-match-ends.rationale: The nonviolent civil-rights tradition holds that methods should embody the goal; inferred and not shared by every strand.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not primitivists.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Only the socialist strand has a view.

production-for-use.rationale: Only the socialist strand has a view.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The anti-capitalist strand might agree, but mainstream anti-racism does not hold this.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship conflicts with equal rights for all; inferred, as Marxist anti-racists rarely foreground it.

taxation-theft.rationale: ICERD assumes a state that funds and enforces equality measures; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: ICERD Art. 4 supports limits beyond direct harm such as racist propaganda, but adherents also value liberty; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: ICERD authorises special measures for racial groups and structural anti-racism analyses group disadvantage; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The civil-rights approach stresses staying and demanding equal rights, not leaving; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers cuts against rights-based equal treatment; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: The structural analysis holds that formal freedoms mean little without material means; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents tend to reject this critique, which is often used against anti-racism; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: ICERD calls racial-superiority doctrines scientifically false and race is widely treated as socially constructed; adherents reject genetic explanations of group differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Anti-racism relies on individual equal suffrage under ICERD Art. 5(c); inferred.

total-state.rationale: Total state direction contradicts the civil-liberty protections in ICERD Art. 5; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth rhetoric is tied to racial nationalism, which anti-racism opposes; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Anti-colonialism is linked to anti-racism, so expansion is opposed; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Hierarchical personal rule is incompatible with equality before the law; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Forced labour recalls slavery and colonial labour, which anti-racists oppose; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Critical strands say supposedly neutral rules preserve dominance, but this is not a general anti-racist epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: ICERD rests on universal human dignity and equality, though adherents also stress cultural recognition; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Structural anti-racists stress group-differentiated interests, but liberal ones appeal to common good; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents are divided; the article notes contested scope even about antisemitism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Only the socialist strand has a view.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on choice versus integration.

rule-by-example.rationale: Anti-racism relies on laws and enforcement, not the moral example of rulers; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial movements are linked to anti-racism in the source; inferred as a general principle.

force-without-un.rationale: ICERD is an expression of multilateral norms, so unilateral force is inferred to be disfavoured.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religious civil-rights strands and secular strands differ.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: ICERD Art. 1(2) allows citizen/non-citizen distinctions but adherents generally dislike welfare chauvinism; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements are commonly criticised as racially disparate in effect; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Adherents prize cultural heritage of oppressed groups, though not statements about sacrificing it; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-colonial strands may favour this; the rest are indifferent.

workers-nation.rationale: Socialist anti-racists stress international solidarity; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Kendi links racism with patriarchy, and equal rights are a common anti-racist commitment; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: ICERD Article 3 condemns racial segregation and apartheid and requires states to eradicate them.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Only the socialist strand holds this.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Environmental racism concerns suggest opposition; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Anti-racism values cultural recognition and opposes demands to abandon identity; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: The source describes the replacement idea as a white-nationalist conspiracy theory, which anti-racism opposes.

proportional-representation.rationale: It tends to improve minority representation; inferred and not a stated demand.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-colonial critiques of imposing one's system on others; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Kendi links racism with patriarchy, and structural analysis is a natural extension; not a core racial claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is associated with racial doctrine, which ICERD condemns; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for state violence against minorities is a common demand; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Anti-racism expects the state to prohibit and remedy discrimination by private actors (ICERD Art. 2(1)(d)).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: ICERD calls racial barriers repugnant, guarantees choice of spouse, and tells states to discourage racial division.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of treatment and rights for all people is the basic claim of anti-racism and of ICERD's preamble.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Dispossession of Indigenous peoples is treated as institutional racism and anti-colonialism is linked to anti-racism; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d)(vii) lists freedom of religion among protected rights; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(c) guarantees equal political participation and universal equal suffrage, reflecting government by consent.

population-transfer.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d) protects freedom of residence and the right to remain in or return to one's country, which forced transfer violates.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: King's nonviolence leans this way, but adherents accept legal force and some accept armed resistance; split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Racial-struggle doctrines are condemned by ICERD, though economic competition is not addressed; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: ICERD Art. 4(b) calls for banning organisations promoting racial discrimination, which is a narrower case than the statement.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Structural anti-racism treats unaccountable power over minorities as unfreedom; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Independent courts to ensure equal treatment (Art. 5(a)) imply checks on power; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only a few Marxist anti-racists endorse it; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Structural analysis connects race with disadvantage, so priority to the poor is broadly favoured; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Direct action and labour alliances are part of the tradition; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The structural view locates poverty in institutions, not population; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: ICERD Art. 2(1)(e) encourages multiracial organisations and discourages racial division; adherents reject this claim.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Equal protection under the law is central to ICERD and the civil-rights tradition; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: ICERD protects freedom of opinion and expression (Art. 5(d)(viii)); inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; inferred opposition to partisan control of force.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: ICERD lets states set citizenship rules but adherents prefer inclusive naturalisation; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: International oversight is welcomed, but supranational union is not addressed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrated executive power sits poorly with checks protecting minorities; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by a religious hierarchy conflicts with equal political rights; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Only some socialist and anti-colonial strands hold this.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: ICERD protects expression, though Art. 4 limits racist propaganda; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; inferred opposition to entrenched power.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing discrimination is a focus, but abolishing renting is not an anti-racist demand; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed-defence traditions exist but are not central; split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Adherents are often university-linked and reject this; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: ICERD condemns superiority doctrines among ethnic groups, and cultural revalorisation movements are part of anti-racism.

death-penalty.rationale: Racial disparities in capital sentencing make adherents opponents; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not racial, but adherents generally favour inclusive curricula; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Adherents defer to scientific consensus; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship tends toward ethnic membership, which adherents dislike; ICERD Art. 1 covers descent as a ground of discrimination.

minority-language-support.rationale: ICERD special measures in cultural fields and recognition of minority culture support this; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Freedom of religion is protected but adherents differ on exemptions.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-capitalist strands favour debt relief; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial strands of anti-racism treat political independence without economic change as incomplete; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Civil and political rights must be enjoyed without racial distinction; inferred opposition to trading them for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Linked to anti-colonial demands and reparations arguments; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Kendi's capitalism critique and the anti-capitalist strand support limiting property for social ends; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental-justice framing favours caution on risks to minority communities; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anti-colonialism is linked to anti-racism; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; religious and secular adherents differ.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Self-determination sympathies make adherents reluctant to endorse coercion; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine hereditary status is the opposite of equal worth; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Seen as regressive in effect on the racial wealth gap; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Race is treated as socially constructed and group differences as environmental, though this answers a broader psychological claim.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(a) requires equality before tribunals and Art. 2(1)(a) binds all public authorities to the obligation.

leader-cult.rationale: Not addressed; inferred distaste for personality cults.

land-redistribution.rationale: The source reports criticism of Zimbabwe's land seizures framed as anti-racist, so adherents are split.

refugee-return.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d)(ii) protects the right to return to one's country; inferred for descendants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ethnic claims to territory sit poorly with ICERD's rejection of ethnic hierarchy; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(d)(vii) lists freedom of thought, conscience and religion; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsion on women conflicts with equality; adherents differ on dress laws generally, so low.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ancestry-based unity runs against ICERD's rejection of racial division; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Recognition of minority culture is supported but integration is also favoured; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: ICERD Art. 2(1)(e) encourages integrationist multiracial movements, and the civil-rights tradition fought for equality at home, though separatist strands differ.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Only the Marxist strand holds this.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(a) requires equal treatment before courts, and anti-racism holds courts must protect minorities from majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Structural-representation logic and the link to patriarchy support this; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Imperial economic blocs are an anti-colonial target; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Labour and environmental justice concerns support this; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The mainstream tradition is nonviolent; some anti-colonial strands differ; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inherited privilege contradicts equal standing, a theme of ICERD; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Anti-racism criticises Eurocentric and nation-centred curricula; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: ICERD preamble condemns colonialism and doctrines of superiority, which rejects rule by supposedly advanced societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed directly; adherents tend to favour critical history; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: ICERD Art. 1(4) allows time-limited special measures and Kendi calls affirmative action antiracist, though some liberal adherents oppose preferences.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-colonialism is linked to anti-racism; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Only a dependency-theory strand holds this.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: ICERD Art. 2(1)(d) requires states to prohibit racial discrimination by persons, groups and organisations, not only by the state.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: ICERD guarantees rights without racial distinction, and entrenchment protects minorities from majorities; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonialism is linked to anti-racism; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Equal access to political participation and public service (Art. 5(c)) favours election over inheritance; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Anti-racism protects minority rights but does not generally endorse individual vetoes; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: King defends resisting unjust law, though this statement concerns breach of constitutional law; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Adherents favour structural remedy over paternalist charity; no clear position.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: King attacks passivity and moderation that wait for justice; inferred to reject withdrawal.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Only anti-colonial and socialist strands hold this.

native-born-offices.rationale: ICERD Art. 5(c) guarantees equal access to public service, and Art. 1 forbids distinctions by descent or origin.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous self-rule is favoured, but leadership over settler descendants is a different claim; split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: ICERD bans racist organisations, so anti-fascism as constitutional value is a natural fit; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The tradition roots itself in abolitionism and treats slavery as the cause; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Contested monuments to figures tied to racism are a common target; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: ICERD assumes universal rights, though anti-colonial strands value self-rule; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Political army roles conflict with equal civilian rights; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Linked to the Kendi view of intersecting capitalism and patriarchy; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Seen as widening wealth gaps; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: ICERD defines discrimination by purpose or effect and Kendi defines a racist policy as any that produces racial inequity, whatever its intent.

single-official-language.rationale: Anti-racism supports equal treatment of ethnic and linguistic groups and opposes forced assimilation, but has no stated language doctrine; inferred from ICERD.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: ICERD requires equal enjoyment of the right to own property regardless of national or ethnic origin, so bans aimed at foreigners lean against it; inferred, and citizenship distinctions are allowed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Anti-racism has no position on consumer culture; the anti-capitalist strand criticises it but the mainstream is indifferent.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-racists backed some armed anti-apartheid movements but the civil-rights tradition is nonviolent, so adherents are split and the issue is not defining.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-racism is anti-colonial and opposes domination of one people by another, so it leans against forced intervention in allies; inferred rather than stated.

missingStatements.text: Governments should review and repeal laws and policies that perpetuate racial discrimination in effect, even where no discriminatory intent exists.
missingStatements.rationale: ICERD defines discrimination by its purpose or effect and Art. 2(1)(c) requires states to amend or nullify laws that create or perpetuate it.

missingStatements.text: A policy should be judged racist if it produces racial inequity, whatever its intent.
missingStatements.rationale: Kendi defines racist policy as any policy that creates inequitable outcomes between racial groups, and the structural view treats intent as secondary.

notes: Liberal anti-racism (colour-blind equal treatment, King's integrationism) and structural anti-racism (Kendi, outcome-based, race-conscious) differ on racial preferences and equal outcomes; the profile takes a moderately race-conscious middle, with ICERD's time-limited special measures as the anchor. The source for King is an excerpt page, not the full letter. Many answers on economics and unrelated issues are low-confidence inferences.
